title.narrative: Fourth Replenishment of the Multilateral Investment Fund - Inter-American Development Bank

description.narrative:
This is the UK’s fourth replenishment to the Multilateral Investment Fund (MIF IV, known as IDB Lab), the innovation and venture capital arm of the Inter-American Development Bank Group (IDBG), supporting early-stage private sector innovation across Latin America and the Caribbean through to 2031. IDB Lab plays a unique role among multilateral development banks, enabling technology and entrepreneurship for poor and vulnerable populations, with a sharpened strategic focus on climate action, gender equality, and Caribbean small island developing states (SIDS). The business case notes that MIF IV will finance 80 operations per year, deploying $1.2 billion and reaching an estimated 47 million people directly. This is a 33% increase in reach per dollar compared to the previous replenishment. The replenishment raises climate finance targets to 40%, with 70% of projects supporting gender equality and 25% promoting diversity. At least 60% of operations will directly support the poor and vulnerable, and 17% of funding will go to Small and Island Countries, reflecting the UK’s priorities in the region.
The UK’s recommended contribution (up to US$3m, not exceeding a 1% burden share) will be matched 1:1 by IDB income and will mobilise further third-party resources, supporting a more sustainable funding model and reducing reliance on donor funds. IDB Lab’s strengthened results framework will track innovation, scalability, and outcomes, including reach, depth, and value of impact. The UK’s negotiating objectives have been met, with greater financial stability, increased strategic focus, and additional support for the Caribbean. This investment aligns with UK priorities on poverty eradication, climate resilience, gender and social inclusion, and strengthens UK influence in shaping innovation and development outcomes in the region, while generating lessons for the wider global financial system.
